product.title: JSON Server
product.summary: Get a full fake REST API from a single JSON or JSON5 file in seconds, for prototyping and mocking front ends without writing a backend.
problems: Mock a REST API for front-end development before the real backend exists
Prototype an app against a fake backend backed by a JSON file
Serve test fixtures over HTTP for end-to-end or integration tests
Quickly expose a JSON file as a CRUD API with filtering, sorting and pagination

workflows.title: Serve a JSON file as a REST API
workflows.description: Point json-server at db.json or db.json5. Every top-level array becomes a collection (GET /posts, GET /posts/:id, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) and every top-level object becomes a singular resource (GET, PUT, PATCH /profile). An index page at / lists the available resources.

workflows.title: Filter, sort, paginate and embed
workflows.description: Query collections with field conditions (field:eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, in, contains, startsWith, endsWith), complex _where JSON, _sort (multiple fields, - for descending), _page and _per_page pagination, and _embed to include related records by foreign key (for example comments with postId).

workflows.title: Write data back to the file
workflows.description: POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests change the in-memory data and rewrite the JSON or JSON5 file. New records get a random base64url id; client-provided ids are ignored. DELETE accepts _dependent to remove related records. Outside production, edits to the file on disk are picked up live.

limitations: Beta v1: usable, but upstream warns to expect breaking changes
No authentication or authorization: anyone who can reach the server can read and change all data
Meant for prototyping and mocking, not production traffic; all data lives in one file and memory
The server listens on every interface whatever --host or HOST says; HOST only changes the URLs it prints
Write requests rewrite the data file in place, so keep a copy of fixtures you want to reuse
Query filters coerce numeric-looking values to numbers, so ?postId=1 does not match string ids such as "1"; use _where={"postId":{"eq":"1"}} to filter on them
Live reload of the data file is turned off when NODE_ENV is production

highlights.title: A REST API from one file
highlights.description: Top-level arrays become collections with full CRUD routes and objects become singular resources, straight from db.json or db.json5.

highlights.title: Rich querying
highlights.description: Field operators (eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, in, contains, startsWith, endsWith), _where JSON with or groups, and multi-field _sort.

highlights.title: Pagination and relations
highlights.description: _page and _per_page return page metadata with the data; _embed includes related records found by foreign key.

highlights.title: Persists and live-reloads
highlights.description: Writes are saved back to the file, and edits you make to the file are picked up without restarting.

highlights.title: Static files included
highlights.description: Serves ./public automatically, plus any directories passed with -s, so a front end and its mock API can share one server.

setup.title: Create the data file
setup.description: Create db.json (or db.json5) with your resources: top-level arrays of objects with string ids become collections, top-level objects become singular resources. fixtures/db.json is a working example. Add "$schema": "./node_modules/json-server/schema.json" for editor validation.

verify.description: The file parses as JSON or JSON5

setup.title: Start the server
setup.description: Run npx json-server db.json (or node lib/bin.js db.json after pnpm build in this repository). Use -p or PORT to change the port (default 3000) and -s to serve extra static directories.

commands.run: pnpm install && pnpm build && node lib/bin.js fixtures/db.json

verify.description: GET http://localhost:3000/ returns the index page listing your resources

core.description: The node:test suite covers the HTTP app, the service layer (find, filter, sort, paginate, embed, create, update, patch, delete with dependents), where-clause parsing and matching, and the normalized file adapter, all on in-test fixtures. Typecheck runs tsc over the sources.

probes.description: The index page lists the fixture resources
A collection returns every fixture record
A record is found by id
A field condition filters the collection
Pagination returns page metadata and one item
A top-level object is served as a singular resource
POST creates a record and returns it with a generated id
The created record is persisted and found by a contains filter
PATCH updates one field of a record
A deleted record returns a JSON 404
An unknown resource returns a JSON 404

storage: One local JSON or JSON5 data file chosen on the command line, held in memory and rewritten on every write request
collected: None by the server itself; it stores whatever clients send to it

customizationPoints.description: Replace the fixture data with your own resources, or pass any JSON or JSON5 file on the command line
Change the built-in index page, or replace it entirely by adding public/index.html
Files in public/ are served as static assets alongside the API

replacedContent: Nothing was replaced: this is the open-source project as maintained upstream; the fixtures are upstream's synthetic sample data
assumptions: Upstream identity is kept: package.json author, LICENSE copyright and the fixture profile name belong to typicode
The README lists upstream's sponsors, and .github/FUNDING.yml and the index page link to typicode's GitHub Sponsors
GitHub Actions workflows from upstream run CI on push and publish to npm on GitHub releases; the publish workflow needs your own npm trusted publishing setup
A husky pre-commit hook runs the tests; it is installed by the prepare script
Node.js 22.12 or newer; the TypeScript sources run directly with type stripping in tests and are compiled to lib/ by pnpm build

costs.description: Running JSON Server locally or on your own host
costs.assumptions: Open-source and self-hosted; it uses no paid services. Any hosting you choose has its own pricing.
